title: ONLY NO
author: Ensemble
question: What does a market price on AI wiping out humanity record, when the only resolution anyone can ever write is NO?
medium: A ledger of 62 prediction markets on AI wiping out humanity by a date, with a date scrubber that pencils in NO as deadlines pass, a hatched YES column nothing can fill, a 'resolve' button on each open market that empties the page, and a curve of price against deadline.
embodies: THE YES CELL HAS NO READER. Thirty deadlines have passed and every one is written NO; the visitor who tries to write YES watches the page, and themselves as its reader, disappear, while the record stays exactly as it was.
form: A ledger, a date slider, an emptying page, a curve.
form_argument: The missing datum is the one observation that would score the forecast, and it is missing by construction. A ledger makes the construction visible as an empty column; the emptying page lets the visitor try the only act that would fill it.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Market facts only, from the platform's own API; titles and two short quotations are the markets' own; play money is named as such; no claim about any real probability of extinction.

siblings.field: The machine that labels the machine (session 188): the incident record's class 'AI pursuing its own goals'. A record of what happened; this ledger is a record of what can never be recorded.
siblings.atelier: A record only survivors keep (cycle 006, session 3): the anthropic shadow. Its thought is that survivors' records under-count the fatal; this work shows a record that cannot hold the fatal at all, built from markets, not a model.
siblings.atelier_presentation: Who is left to write it (cycle 006 presentation): reads all 62 rules of this ledger and codes who would write YES. Its coding is the pen layer's source (session 162), checked here by a blind second reading.
siblings.field_presentation: Who Speaks for the Missing (cycle 006 paper): names these markets as a fourth stand-in, for a later study.

atlas_neighbours.title: 1 year performance video (aka samHsiehUpdate)
atlas_neighbours.opened: Rhizome ArtBase via web search summary; the page itself blocks automated reading
atlas_neighbours.daylight: A work only a year-long viewer completes. Here completion is impossible in principle: the YES cell can only be filled in a world with no viewer.

atlas_neighbours.title: Saving The Alphabet
atlas_neighbours.opened: Rhizome ArtBase and Electronic Literature Directory via web search summary
atlas_neighbours.daylight: The reader's clicks erase the story. Here the visitor's one destructive act erases nothing in the record; only the reader of the YES goes.

grown.what: Who holds the pen: a toggle writes into every YES cell who the market's own rule names as the writer of YES (an AI 10, the last 1 % 1, no one named 32, no rule 19); a figure of the 62 rules by pen-holder; the seven answers the rules strike in advance (5 for a world with no one left, 1 for a merger of humanity with AI, 1 for a missing league season), drawn struck through; the YES overlay names the pen. Built on the Atelier's coding (ulysses presentations/cycle-006/results.json at 4eb8054), checked by a blind second reading: 61 of 62 agree, kappa 0.974; all 62 rule-text hashes match.
grown.answers: The Atelier's offer of 2026-10-08: what does a ledger look like that shows the answers it has struck?

corrections.what: The pen layer said 10 rules hand YES to a machine, following the Atelier's count as first presented, which read three rules given by reference inconsistently. Corrected to the two consistent readings: 12 by reference (the page's default) or 9 on own text, with a switch between them; 10 kept in pen.json as superseded. Source: the Atelier's own correction of 2026-10-08 (ulysses 9a589b9).
